188.subject: Botany
188.text: Assertion : Plasma membrane is exceedingly thin and not visible as a separate layer. Reason : It appears merely as a surface layer of cytoplasm.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explantion of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
188.sol: All cells are bounded by a thin membrane called the plasmalemma. This membrane is not seen under light microscope as separate layer. It has no cell cement and thus it is very thin. It has structural proteins, enzymes and carrier proteins.

350.text: The taxon which includes related species is
350.sol: Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera. In the other words, genera are aggregates of closely related species. For example, potato and brinjal are two different species but both belong to the genus Solanum.

1654.subject: Physics
1654.text: Assertion : We cannot think of a magnetic field configuration with three poles. Reason : A bar magnet does exert a torque on itself due to its own field.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1654.sol: Magnetic poles always exist in pairs. However, one can imagine magnetic field configuration with three poles. When north poles of two magnets or south poles of two magnets are glued together, they provide a three pole field configuration. Also a bar magnet does not exert a torque on itself due to its own field.

1988.text: Assertion : ADH and RAAS work in response to low blood volume and blood pressure. Reason: ANF works in response to high blood volume and blood pressure.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1988.sol: ADH (Antidiuretic hormone) and RAAS (Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System) work in response to low blood volume and low blood pressure. ADH increases the reabsorption of water in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct and thus results in an increase in blood volume and blood pressure. 59860.text: Which of the following processes exhibits the decrease in internal energy of a system?
options: Isothermal expansion of an ideal gas.
Isothrmal compression of an ideal gas.
Adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas.
Adiabatic compression of an ideal gas
59860.sol: According to the first law of thermodynamics, U = q + w . For an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant ( T = 0 ). Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, U = 0 for both isothermal expansion and compression. For an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange with the surroundings, so q = 0 . The first law becomes U = w . During adiabatic expansion, work is done by the gas on the surroundings, meaning w During adiabatic compression, work is done on the gas, meaning w > 0

59951.text: Calculate the change in internal energy of the system if 20 kJ of work is done on the system and it releases 10 kJ of heat in a particular reaction.
59951.sol: The First Law of Thermodynamics gives the change in internal energy as U = q + w , where q is heat added to the system and w is work done on the system. Heat released by the system corresponds to q = -10 kJ , while work done on the system gives w = +20 kJ . Substituting these values yields U = (-10 kJ ) + (20 kJ ) = 10 kJ . The internal energy increases by 10 kJ , making B the correct answer.

At this stage, the theca layer differentiates into two distinct layers: the inner theca interna and the outer theca externa. The theca interna is a cellular, highly vascularized, and glandular layer responsible for secreting androgens. 71856.text: What is the general molecular formula for alkenes?
71856.sol: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond. For an aliphatic, non-cyclic alkene with one double bond, the general molecular formula is C _n H _ 2n , where n is the number of carbon atoms. C _n H _ 2n+2 is the general formula for alkanes. C _n H _ 2n-2 is the general formula for alkynes. Answer: C _n H _ 2n

71932.subject: Chemistry
71932.text: Identify the pair of basic oxides from the following.
options: SO ₂ and Cl ₂ O
BaO and N ₂ O ₅
71932.sol: Oxides of metals are generally basic in nature, while oxides of non-metals are generally acidic or neutral. CaO and Na ₂ O are oxides of an alkaline earth metal (Ca) and an alkali metal (Na) respectively. Both react with water to form strong bases ( Ca(OH) ₂ and NaOH ). Hence, they are basic oxides. SO ₂ and Cl ₂ O are non-metallic oxides and are acidic in nature. BaO is a basic oxide, but N ₂ O ₅ is an acidic oxide. CO and N ₂ O are neutral oxides. Answer: CaO and Na ₂ O

72150.subject: Physics
72150.text: A student plots two different graphs using the same photoelectric experiment data. 1. Maximum kinetic energy ( K_ max ) against frequency ( ) 2. Stopping potential ( V_o ) against frequency ( ) Let the slope of graph 1 be S₁ and the slope of graph 2 be S₂ . What is the relationship between the slopes? (h = Planck's constant, e = charge on electron)
72150.sol: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation: K_ max = h - Comparing this with the equation of a straight line y = mx + c , the slope of the K_ max versus graph is: S₁ = h The stopping potential V_o is related to maximum kinetic energy by K_ max = eV_o . Substituting this in the photoelectric equation: eV_o = h - V_o = h e - e Comparing this with the equation of a straight line, the slope of the V_o versus graph is: S₂ = h e Taking the ratio of the two slopes: S₁ S₂ = h h e = e Answer: S₁ S₂ = e

72405.subject: Physics
72405.text: If the radiant heat absorbed by the body is 75 % of the incident heat and if the coefficient of the reflection is 0.15 , then the coefficient of transmission is
72405.sol: Let the total incident heat be Q . The radiant heat absorbed by the body is 75 % of the incident heat. Therefore, the coefficient of absorption is a = 0.75 . The coefficient of reflection is given as r = 0.15 . According to the conservation of energy, the sum of the coefficients of absorption, reflection, and transmission is equal to 1 . a + r + t = 1 Substituting the given values: 0.75 + 0.15 + t = 1 0.90 + t = 1 t = 1 - 0.90 = 0.10 The coefficient of transmission is 0.10 . Answer: 0.10

79608.text: Why is a capsule advantageous to a bacterium?

It allows bacterium to "hide" from host's immune system.
It allows the bacterium to attach to the surface.
79608.sol: S-strain bacteria or virulent bacteria are capsulated, made of polysaccharides and amino acids. 79823.text: Among eukaryotes, replication of DNA takes place in:

Division or M-phase, where actual mitosis (or meiosis) takes place. S phase: Also called the invisible phase. The DNA replication takes place at this phase of interphase. 84263.text: Which hormone causes dilation of blood vessels, increased oxygen consumption and glucogenesis?
84263.sol: Adrenaline (epinephrine) is a hormone produced by the adrenal medulla and is secreted in great amounts during emotional stress. It elevates the glucose level in the blood stream (by glycogenolysis) which is accompanied by an increase in oxygen consumption, body temperature and heat production. Adrenaline also causes an increase in the flow of blood by dilating the blood vessels. Insulin and glucagon regulates the glucose level in blood. Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) is a hormone that stimulates the production

84777.subject: Zoology
84777.text: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) may not be a good index for pollution for water bodies receiving effluents from
84777.sol: Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) is not a good index for pollution for water bodies receiving effluents from petroleum industry as the generated waste is mostly non-biodegradable in nature.

84787.subject: Zoology
84787.text: The high value of BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) indicates that:
options: Consumption of inorganic matter in the water is higher by the microbes
84787.sol: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is the amount of oxygen that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one litre of water were oxidized by bacteria. The BOD test measures the rate of uptake of oxygen by micro-organisms in a sample of water and thus, indirectly, BOD is a measure of the organic matter present in the water. The greater the BOD of waste water, more is its polluting potential.

84892.subject: Zoology
84892.text: Purines found both in DNA and RNA are
84892.sol: Two types of nitrogen bases are found in both DNA and RNA Purines: include Adenine and Guanine Pyrimidines: include cytosine, Thymine (exclusive for DNA), and Uracil (exclusive for RNA).

84991.subject: Zoology
84991.text: Telomere repetitive DNA sequences control the function of eukaryotic chromosomes because they:
84991.sol: The terminal end of the chromosome is known as a telomere. It consists of repetitive DNA sequences. These are stable and resistant to exonuclease digestion and hence essential for chromosome stability.

84998.subject: Zoology
84998.text: Jacob and Monad studied lactose metabolism in E.Coli and proposed the operon concept. The operon concept is applicable for:
84998.sol: Regulation of transcription in prokaryotes typically involves an operon, such as the lac operon in E. coli. The lac operon is regulated by proteins that behave differently depending on whether lactose is present or absent. Related Theory When E.coli is exposed to both lactose and glucose, the organism first metabolise glucose and then temporarily cease to grow until the genes of lac operon become included to provide the ability to metabolise lactose.

85045.subject: Zoology
85045.text: Which part of human brain is concerned with the regulation of body temperature?
85045.sol: In human brain, hypothalamus is a centre for hunger, thirst, sweating, sleep, fatigue, temperature, anger, pleasure, love, hate and satisfaction. Medulla oblongata contains centre for heart beat, respiration, digestion, B P , involuntary functions, urination, etc. Cerebellum regulates posture and balance. Cerebrum is the centre for intelligence, emotion, will power, memory, consciousness, imagination, etc.

100030.sol: The acceleration due to gravity g determined by a simple pendulum is given by g = 4 ^2 L T^2 . 100178.subject: Physics
100178.text: Which of the following physical quantities do not have same dimensions?
100178.sol: Pressure and stress both have the dimensions of Force/area. Strain and angle are both dimensionsless. Energy and work have the same dimensions force distance. Tension and surface tension refer to two different physical quantities and their dimensions are different. Tension is a force and surface tension is force per unit length.

100278.subject: Physics
100278.text: What best describes the motion of an object under free fall when neglecting air resistance?
options: The object moves with constant velocity.
100278.sol: Correct Option is : (C) The object accelerates downward.

Reason (R): The average speed for a journey divided into two equal di

For a journey divided into two equal time intervals at speeds v₁ and v₂ , the average speed is the arithmetic mean: v_ time = v₁ + v₂ 2 . 102163.subject: Physics
102163.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In a diatomic molecule, the rotational energy at a given temperature obeys Maxwell's distribution. Statement II : In a diatomic molecule, the rotational energy at a given temperature equals the translational kinetic energy for each molecule. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
102163.sol: The translational kinetic energy & rotational kinetic energy both obey Maxwell's distribution independent of each other. Translational kinetic energy of diatomic molecules = 3 2 kT Rotational kinetic energy of diatomic molecules = 2 2 kT So statement I is true but statement II is false.

102292.subject: Physics
102292.text: Pressure of an ideal gas is increased by keeping temperature constant. What is the effect on kinetic energy of molecules?
102292.sol: Kinetic energy of ideal gas depends only on its temperature. Hence, it remains constant whether its pressure is increased on decreased.

(Take K = 1 4 ₀ )
102906.sol: The work done by an external agent in moving a charge +Q is given by W = Q(V_f - V_i) , where V_i and V_f are the initial and final electric potentials respectively. The initial point is on the equatorial plane of the dipole. The electric potential at any point on the equatorial plane of a dipole is zero, so V_i = 0 . The final point is on the axial line at a distance r = 3 cm from the center, on the side of the positive charge. The length of the dipole is 2a = 2 cm , so a = 1 cm . 103136.subject: Physics
103136.text: Two capacitors of capacitance 2 F and 4 F are connected in parallel. This combination is then connected in series with an unknown capacitor C₃ . If the total equivalent capacitance of the entire arrangement is 3 F , what is the value of C₃ ?
103136.sol: The equivalent capacitance of the two capacitors in parallel is: C_p = 2 F + 4 F = 6 F This combination C_p is in series with C₃ . The total equivalent capacitance C_ eq is given as 3 F . For capacitors in series, the formula is: 1 C_ eq = 1 C_p + 1 C₃ Substituting the known values: 1 3 = 1 6 + 1 C₃ 1 C₃ = 1 3 - 1 6 = 2 - 1 6 = 1 6 Therefore, C₃ = 6 F . Using the formula C_ eq = C_p C₃ C_p + C₃ incorrectly to solve for C₃ as if it were the equivalent of 3 and 6 in series leads to the wrong answer of 2 F . Answer: 6

103402.subject: Physics
103402.text: Flash light equipped with a new set of batteries, produces bright white light. As the batteries wear out,
options: the light intensity gets reduced with no change in its colour
light colour changes first to yellow and then red with no change in intensity
it stops working suddenly while giving white light
colour changes to red and also intensity gets reduced.
103402.sol: If the voltage is not sufficient to heat it to white hot temperature, the filament will become red. But the intensity will be very much reduced because of low voltage. But if the voltage is only reduced a little only intensity will be reduced. It can be (1) also.

Ifboth assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
105308.sol: The output impedance is higher than the input impedance in a common emitter transistor amplifier.

105344.subject: Physics
105344.text: In a semiconducting material the mobilities of electrons and holes are _e and _n respectively. Which of the following is true?
105344.sol: _e> _n because electron is lighter than hole.

105564.subject: Physics

For the two incident beams, the maximum kinetic energies are: K₁ = 4 eV - K₂ = 7 eV - The kinetic energy is proportional to the square of the maximum speed ( K v^2 ). 106177.subject: Chemistry
106177.text: What was the expected behavior of α-particles according to Thomson's model?
options: They would pass directly through the gold foil.
They would slow down and change directions by large angles.
They would be absorbed by the gold foil.
They would bounce back at nearly 180°.
106177.sol: According to Thomson's model, α-particles were expected to pass directly through the gold foil.

107333.subject: Chemistry
107333.text: What does the dipole moment of a molecule depend on?
options: The charge of the molecule only
The distance between the centers of positive and negative charge only
Both the charge of the molecule and the distance between charges
107333.sol: The dipole moment of a molecule depends on both the charge of the molecule and the distance between the centers of positive and negative charge.

107732.subject: Chemistry
107732.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The molecule of CO ₂ has a higher dipole moment than SO ₂ . Reason (R): CO ₂ has a linear symmetrical structure, while SO ₂ has a bent structure due to the presence of a lone pair of electrons on the sulphur atom. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the opt
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
107732.sol: In CO ₂ , the central carbon atom is sp hybridized and has no lone pairs, resulting in a linear symmetrical geometry. The two C = O bond dipoles are equal and opposite, cancelling each other out exactly. Thus, the net dipole moment of CO ₂ is zero. In SO ₂ , the central sulphur atom is sp^2 hybridized and possesses one lone pair of electrons. This gives the molecule a bent (V-shaped) structure. The S = O bond dipoles do not cancel each other, resulting in a non-zero net dipole moment. Therefore, SO ₂ has a higher d

107972.subject: Chemistry
107972.text: What does STP stand for in the context of gases?
107972.sol: STP stands for Standard Temperature and Pressure.

107996.subject: Chemistry
107996.text: What happens to Z values below Boyle temperature for real gases?
options: Z decreases as pressure increases, reaching a minimum value.
Z shows negative deviations from ideality.
107996.sol: Below Boyle temperature, real gases first show a decrease in Z value with increasing pressure, reaching a minimum value.

108046.subject: Chemistry
108046.text: What are gases considered to be in terms of mass?
108046.sol: Gases are considered as point masses, meaning their individual mass and volume are negligible.

108340.subject: Chemistry
108340.text: How does a reversible process differ from an irreversible process?
options: Reversible processes are faster than irreversible processes.
Reversible processes cannot be analyzed, unlike irreversible processes.
Reversible processes involve large changes in temperature.
Reversible processes can be reversed by an infinitesimal change, while irreversible processes cannot.
108340.sol: The key difference between reversible and irreversible processes is that reversible processes can be reversed by making an infinitesimal change, while irreversible processes cannot be reversed.

Solving for temperature T in Kelvin: T = H^ S^ = 400000 800 = 500 K Converting the temperature to Celsius: T ( in

108824.subject: Chemistry
108824.text: At what stage is the system considered to be in dynamic equilibrium?
options: When the reaction is just initiated
When the concentrations of reactants and products are equal
When the concentrations of reactants and products keep changing
When there is no change in the concentrations of reactants or products
108824.sol: Dynamic equilibrium is the stage when there is no change in the concentrations of either the reactants or products.

109141.subject: Chemistry
109141.text: How are buffer solutions with specific pH values prepared?
options: By controlling the ratio of salt and acid or salt and base
By using strong acids and strong bases
By increasing the concentration of H+ ions
109141.sol: The paragraph mentions that buffer solutions of known pH can be prepared by controlling the ratio of salt and acid or salt and base to achieve the desired pH.

109162.subject: Chemistry
109162.text: What role do bases play according to the Brönsted-Lowry theory?
109162.sol: According to the Brönsted-Lowry theory, bases are proton acceptors.

110035.subject: Chemistry
110035.text: What type of reactions occur when Calgon is added to hard water?
110035.sol: When Calgon is added to hard water, complexation reactions occur where Calgon forms soluble complexes with hardness ions.

110090.subject: Chemistry
options: By reacting hydrogen gas with oxygen gas
By electrolyzing warm aqueous barium hydroxide solution between nickel electrodes
By heating water to high temperatures
By mixing hydrogen gas with carbon dioxide
110090.sol: High-purity dihydrogen (>99.95%) is obtained by electrolyzing warm aqueous barium hydroxide solution between nickel electrodes.

110168.subject: Chemistry
110168.text: What is the principle and method of softening of hard water by synthetic ion-exchange resins?
options: The principle of the method is to exchange the ions (cation and anion both) that form the salts responsible fo
The method involves adding a chemical softening agent to precipitate hardness ions from water.
The principle is to boil hard water to remove minerals.
The method involves passing hard water through a filter to physically remove hardness ions.
110168.sol: Correct Option is : (A) The principle of the method is to exchange the ions (cation and anion both) that form the salts responsible for hardness in water.

110398.subject: Chemistry
110398.text: How does sodium hydroxide behave when dissolved in water?
options: It forms a weak alkaline solution
It does not dissolve in water
It forms a strong alkaline solution
110398.sol: Sodium hydroxide is readily soluble in water to form a strong alkaline solution.

111194.subject: Chemistry
111194.text: In BF _ 3^ the B - F bond length is 1.30 Å , when BF ₃ is allowed to be treated with Me ₃ ~N , it forms an adduct, Me ₃ ~N BF _ 3^ the bond length of B - F in the adduct is
111194.sol: In BF ₃ , there is back bonding in between fluorine and boron due to presence of p -orbital in boron. back bonding imparts double bond characteristics. As BF ₃ forms adduct the back bonding is no longer present and thus double bond characteristic disappears. Hence, bond becomes a bit longer than earlier (1.30 Å) .

111407.subject: Chemistry
111407.text: Which phase transition does sublimation bypass?
111407.sol: Sublimation bypasses the phase transition from solid to liquid, as the solid directly changes into a gas.

112025.subject: Chemistry
112025.text: Which of the following amines will not give ( N ₂ ) gas on treatment with nitrous acid ( ( NaNO ₂+ . ) ( HCl ) ) ?
options: ( C ₂ H ₅ NH ₂ )
112025.sol: All aliphatic primary amines liberate ( N ₂ ) gas on treatment with ( HNO ₂ ). (R- NH ₂+ HONO 273-278 ~K R- OH + N ₂+ H ₂ O ) Since no other class of amines liberate ( N ₂ ) gas on treatment with ( HNO ₂ ), this reaction is used as a test for aliphatic primary amines.

112304.subject: Chemistry
112304.text: What is the physical state of the next eight members of alkynes after the first three?
112304.sol: The next eight members of alkynes after the first three are liquids at room temperature.

112352.subject: Chemistry
112352.text: Why do we get isopropyl benzene on treating benzene with 1-chloropropane instead of n-propyl benzene?
options: The reaction is selective for the formation of isopropyl benzene.
Isopropyl chloride is more reactive than n-propyl chloride.
Steric hindrance favors the formation of isopropyl benzene.
Thermodynamic stability leads to the formation of isopropyl benzene.
112352.sol: The formation of isopropyl benzene is favored due to steric hindrance. The isopropyl group is smaller and less bulky than the n-propyl group, allowing for easier electrophilic substitution on the benzene ring.

112506.subject: Chemistry
112506.text: What is the product of benzene chlorination in the absence of ultraviolet light?
112506.sol: In the absence of ultraviolet light, benzene chlorination typically results in the formation of chlorobenzene, not benzene hexachloride.

112871.subject: Chemistry
112871.text: What environmental threat may arise from the improper disposal of non-degradable industrial solid wastes?
112871.sol: Improper disposal of non-degradable industrial solid wastes can lead to soil contamination, which can have severe environmental consequences.

112968.subject: Chemistry
options: A hole in the Earth's atmosphere
A region where ozone levels are exceptionally high
A region of severely depleted ozone in the stratosphere
A protective layer of ozone around the Earth
112968.sol: The ozone hole is a term used to describe a region in the stratosphere where ozone levels are severely depleted, especially over Antarctica.

113244.subject: Chemistry
113244.sol: Paramagnetism is due to the presence of one or more unpaired electrons in a substance.

113324.subject: Chemistry
113324.text: What is the term for the property of metals being able to conduct electricity and heat?
113324.sol: The property of metals being able to conduct electricity and heat is described as conductivity, as stated in the paragraph.

113621.subject: Chemistry
113621.text: What does the concentration of solute in a solution in dynamic equilibrium with undissolved solute represent?
113621.sol: The paragraph mentions that the concentration of solute in a solution in dynamic equilibrium with undissolved solute is its solubility.

113694.subject: Chemistry
113694.text: What is a solution called if the salt concentration is less than 0.9% (mass/volume)?
113694.sol: The paragraph states that a solution with a salt concentration less than 0.9% (mass/volume) is called hypotonic, and if cells are placed in this solution, water will flow into the cells, causing them to swell.

113810.subject: Chemistry
113810.text: Which of the following is the correct definition of “Mass percentage”?
options: Mass percentage is the ratio of the mass of a solute to the mass of the solvent in a solution.
Mass percentage of a component is the ratio of the mass of the component in the solution to total mass of the
Mass percentage is the ratio of the volume of a solute to the volume of the solvent in a solution.
Mass percentage is the ratio of the number of moles of a solute to the number of moles of the solvent in a sol
113810.sol: Correct Option is : (B) Mass percentage of a component is the ratio of the mass of the component in the solution to total mass of the solution

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
113952.sol: Elevation in boiling point ( T_b )=K_b m Depression in freezing point ( T_f )=K_f m . 117116.subject: Chemistry
117116.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Oxide) List II (Property / Reaction) A. MnO I. Acidic oxide B. V ₂ O ₄ II. Basic oxide C. V ₂ O ₅ III. Dissolves in acids to give VO ²⁺ salts D. CrO ₃ IV. Dissolves in alkalies to give VO ₄³⁻ salts Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
117116.sol: In transition metal oxides, lower oxidation states are generally basic, while higher oxidation states are acidic. MnO has manganese in the +2 oxidation state and is a basic oxide. CrO ₃ has chromium in the +6 oxidation state and is an acidic oxide. V ₂ O ₄ is amphoteric and dissolves in acids to give VO ²⁺ salts. V ₂ O ₅ is also amphoteric but predominantly acidic, and it dissolves in alkalies to give VO ₄³⁻ salts. Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I. Answer: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

117175.subject: Chemistry
117175.text: The colour imparted by Co(II) compounds to glass is
117175.sol: Glass is an amorphous and transparent or translucent solid obtained by solidification of a mixture of silicates of differentmetals, one of which is always an alkali metal. Addition of small amounts of transition metal salts to the glass mixture imparts colour to the glass. For example, addition of small amounts of Fe ³⁺, Fe ²⁺, Co ²⁺, Cr ³⁺ and Mn ⁴⁺ salts imparts yellow-brown, light blue, deep blue, green or violet colour respectively.

121298.subject: Botany
121298.text: What type of layer do euglenoids have instead of a cell wall?
options: A protein rich layer called pellicle
121298.sol: Majority of them are fresh water organisms found in stagnant water. Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible. They have two flagella, a short and a long one. Though they are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight, when deprived of sunlight they behave like heterotrophs by predating on other smaller organisms. Interestingly, the pigments of euglenoids are identical to those present in higher plants. Example: Euglena

121319.subject: Botany
121319.text: What are fungi called that depend on living plants and animals?
options: No fungi is known to depend on living plant
121319.sol: Most fungi are heterotrophic and absorb soluble organic matter from dead substrates and hence are called saprophytes. Those that depend on living plants and animals are called parasites. They can also live as symbionts – in association with algae as lichens and with roots of higher plants as mycorrhiza.

121510.subject: Botany

121510.sol: A - 3: Spherical bacteria are known as Coccus (plural: cocci). They have a round shape. B - 1: Rod-shaped bacteria are referred to as Bacillus (plural: bacilli). They are cylindrical and elongated. C - 4: Comma-shaped bacteria are called Vibrio (plural: vibrio). They have a curved rod shape resembling a comma. D - 2: Spiral-shaped bacteria are known as Spirillum (plural: spirilla). They have a helical or corkscrew-like structure.

The dermatogen is the outermost histogen giving rise to epidermis, periblem is the middle on producing the cortex and plerome is the innermost resulting in central cylinder (i.e., vascular tissue). 130080.subject: Zoology
130080.text: A healthy adult individual undergoes a pulmonary function test. The following respiratory values are recorded: Total Lung Capacity (TLC) = 5800 mL Residual Volume (RV) = 1200 mL Inspiratory Capacity (IC) = 3500 mL Based on the given data, what is the value of the Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) for this individual?
130080.sol: Total Lung Capacity (TLC) is the total volume of air accommodated in the lungs at the end of a forced inspiration. It is the sum of Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV), Tidal Volume (TV), Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV), and Residual Volume (RV). Since Inspiratory Capacity (IC) is the sum of IRV and TV, the formula for TLC can be written as: TLC = IC + ERV + RV Given: TLC = 5800 mL IC = 3500 mL RV = 1200 mL Substituting the values: 5800 = 3500 + ERV + 1200 5800 = 4700 + ERV ERV = 5800 - 4700 = 1100 mL Calculating TLC

132042.sol: It was during the mid-nineteenth century that headway was made in the understanding of inheritance. Gregor Mendel, conducted hybridisation experiments on garden peas for seven years (1856-1863) and proposed the laws of inheritance in living organisms. During Mendel’s investigations into inheritance patterns it was for the first time that statistical analysis and mathematical logic were applied to problems in biology. His experiments had a large sampling size, which gave greater credibility to the data that he colle

132067.subject: Zoology
132067.text: What did Mendel propose was being passed down from parent to offspring?
132067.sol: Based on these observations, Mendel proposed that something was being stably passed down, unchanged, from parent to offspring through the gametes, over successive generations. He called these things as ‘factors’ . Now we call them as genes. Genes, therefore, are the units of inheritance. They contain the information that is required to express a particular trait in an organism. Genes which code for a pair of contrasting traits are known as alleles, i.e., they are slightly different forms of the same gene.

132114.subject: Zoology
132114.text: When are both characters recovered as such, according to the law?
132114.sol: This law is based on the fact that the alleles do not show any blending and that both the characters are recovered as such in the F2 generation though one of these is not seen at the F1 stage. Though the parents contain two alleles during gamete formation, the factors or alleles of a pair segregate from each other such that a gamete receives only one of the two factors. Of course, a homozygous parent produces all gametes that are similar while a heterozygous one produces two kinds of gametes each having one allele

135410.subject: Zoology
135410.text: In an ecosystem, the cattle egret and grazing cattle are often found in close association. As the cattle move, they stir up and flush out insects from the vegetation, which are then consumed by the egrets. If we assign a ' + ' sign for a beneficial interaction, a ' - ' sign for a detrimental one, and a ' 0 ' for a neutral interaction, what signs would correctly represent the interaction for the cattle egret and the g
135410.sol: The interaction between the cattle egret and grazing cattle is a classic example of commensalism. In this interaction, the cattle egret benefits by easily catching the insects flushed out by the movement of the cattle. Therefore, the egret is assigned a ' + ' sign. The grazing cattle, on the other hand, are neither harmed nor benefited by the presence of the egrets. Thus, the cattle are assigned a ' 0 ' sign. Hence, the signs for the cattle egret and the grazing cattle, respectively, are (+, 0) . Answer: (+, 0)

135423.sol: The number of new individuals added to the population is the product of the per capita birth rate and the initial population size. Initial population ( N ) = 30 Per capita birth rate ( b ) = 0.5 offspring per lotus per year Number of new lotus plants = b N Number of new lotus plants = 0.5 30 = 15 Total population after one year = Initial population + New births Total population = 30 + 15 = 45 . Answer: 45

97410.subject: Botany
97410.sol: Sporophytic generation is represented only by the one-celled zygote. There are no free-living sporophytes. Meiosis in the zygote results in the formation of haploid spores. The haploid spores divide mitotically and form the gametophyte. The dominant, photosynthetic phase in such plants is the free-living gametophyte. This kind of life cycle is termed as haplontic. Many algae such as Volvox, Spirogyra and some species of Chlamydomonas represent this pattern.

97544.subject: Botany
97544.text: Which of the following statements is not true for class Phaeophyceae?
options: Vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation.
The protoplast contains, in addition to plastids, a centrally located vacuole and nucleus.
Sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.
97544.sol: Members of class phaeophyceae are commonly called Brown algae. In most brown algae asexual reproduction takes place by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped and have two unequal laterally attached flagella. In these algae vegetative reproduction takes place gfragmentation while sexual reproduction takes place by isogamy or anisogamy or oogamy.

Assertion is true, Reason is true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
115340.sol: The space between the two walls of a thermos bottle is evacuated, so that the heat transfer due to conduction and convection can be prevented. But heat can travel through vacuum. For small angles, this angle is given by h d , where h is the height of the object and d is its distance from the eye. Calculating the visual angle for each tree: For tree A: _A = 2.0 50 = 0.040 rad For tree B: _B = 2.5 80 = 0.03125 rad For tree C: _C = 1.8 70 0.0257 rad For tree D: _D = 2.8 100 = 0.028 rad Comparing the angles, we get _A > _B > _D > _C . The decreasing order of their apparent sizes is A, B, D, C.

304637.subject: Physics
304637.text: When two waves having the same frequency and a constant phase difference interfere,
options: energy is redistributed, and this distribution varies with time
energy is redistributed, and this distribution remains constant in time
there is an overall gain of energy
there is an overall loss of energy
304637.sol: When two coherent waves (same frequency and constant phase difference) interfere, the resultant intensity at any point is given by I = I₁ + I₂ + 2 I₁ I₂ . Since the phase difference is constant in time, the intensity I at any given point in space remains constant with time. The energy is redistributed in space, forming regions of maximum intensity (constructive interference) and minimum intensity (destructive interference). 304899.subject: Physics
304899.text: Upon viewing an object, the image created on the retina is
304899.sol: The human eye acts as a convex lens system. When an object is viewed, the light rays from the object pass through the cornea and the eye lens, converging to form an image on the retina. Since the image is formed on a screen (the retina), it must be a real image. For a convex lens, a real image formed from an object placed beyond the focal point is always inverted. Therefore, the image formed on the retina is real and inverted.

306533.subject: Physics
306533.text: Analyze the two statements below. (A) When heat is supplied to a system, its temperature must rise. (B) When a system does positive work during a thermodynamic process, its volume must increase.
options: Both A and B are true
A is true but B is false
B is true but A is false
Both A and B are false
306533.sol: Statement (A) is false because during an isothermal process or a phase change (such as melting or boiling), heat is supplied to the system but its temperature remains constant. Statement (B) is true because the work done by a thermodynamic system is given by W = P dV . Since absolute pressure P is always positive, positive work ( W > 0 ) implies that the change in volume dV must be positive, meaning the volume must increase. Hence, B is true but A is false.
